slides.title: October 2026 was a rough month for developer security
slides.sub: Here is what happened, in plain words. Swipe →

slides.title: PHP had two *critical* security holes
slides.body: They're called PHP2Shell. PHP runs nearly three quarters of the websites in the world.

slides.title: It happens before your code *even runs*
slides.body: PHP2Shell happens while PHP reads the request, so your login can't stop it.

slides.title: Update PHP, then *restart* it
slides.body: Any of these versions (or newer) has the fix. After updating, restart PHP-FPM or Apache.

slides.title: Railway told its users to change their *secret keys*
slides.body: Railway is a platform developers deploy apps on. Someone may have reached customers' environment variables, where those keys live.

slides.title: Zeabur is shutting down after *two breaches*
slides.body: The second one came through an admin token that never expired.

slides.title: Some people found out from their *AI bills*
slides.body: Attackers took AI keys stored in OpenCode. A few bills went over $1,000 for usage people never ran.

slides.title: What you can do with *your keys*
rows: Give every key an expiry date
Give each key only what it needs
slides.body: Three of this month's breaches went for the place developers keep these keys.

cols.v: One hacker used AI agents to break into 100+ company websites.

slides.title: Did you have to patch or change keys this month?
slides.body: I put all of it in one video, in plain words.
